City Council Meeting
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
City Council, Community Development Financing Authority, Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*
February 20, 2012
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 05:04 p.m. , on February 20, 2012, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.
A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00 p.m. on February 16, 2012, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.
*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."
Present:
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Schlicht
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Ury
Absent:
None
Staff Present:
Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
William P Curley III, City Attorney
Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
INVOCATION: Council Member Schlicht
CLOSED SESSION
CS1.
Labor Negotiations - The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations Are the City and City's Unrepresented Employees. The City's Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.
RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE
At the hour of 5:06 p.m., Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council reconvened at 6:03 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.
REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION
City Attorney Bill Curley announced that staff presented various personnel programs, the City Council provided direction, and the matter will be brought back to the Council at a future date.
PRESENTATIONS
Items P1 and P2 were taken out of order.
P2.
Presentation by Saddleback College KSBR 88.5 FM Radio
Terry Wedel, Director of KSBR Radio, thanked the City Council for their support and partnership. Mr. Wedel, along with Gary Bergeson and Kelly Bennet, presented a short video on the KSBR programs and invited the City Council Members and residents to the KSBR Birthday Bash on May 27, 2012.
P1.
Presentation of Award to Deputies Rich Castro, Justin Osterfeld, John Popp, and Ronald Rhodes by Mothers Against Drunk Drivers (MADD)
Lt. Mike Gavin presented the awards on behalf of Mothers Against Drunk Drivers (MADD).
PUBLIC COMMENTS
Hal Brown, M.V.: questioned the high fire hazard severity zone maps and asked about the criteria for including new houses into those zones. He stated that residents do not understand the implications of the high fire hazard severity zone designation.
Erika Schulte, M.V.: speaking on behalf of the administration of the Oxford Preparatory Academy, she thanked the City of Mission Viejo for its support and stated that they are working hard to make sure that their traffic is flowing as safely and efficiently as possible.
Robert Reidel, M.V.: reiterated the comments about Oxford Preparatory Academy and the school administration’s efforts to alleviate traffic issues.
Frank Camilleri, M.V.: speaking as a parent of an Oxford Prep student and resident of Mission Viejo, he announced that the school has formed a task force to address traffic issues and he hopes that the City Council and law enforcement will partner and collaborate with Oxford Prep.
Sharon Cody, M.V.: announced that the Dedicated Animal Welfare Group (DAWG) has reached $1 million in donations and 38,000 animals have been saved because of the Mission Viejo animal shelter.
Bob Hayes, M.V.: discussed the meaning of Presidents Day.
COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS
Item 27 was taken out of order.
Council Member Schlicht
27.
Support of AB 1455 (Harkey) High Speed Rail Lemon Law
Assemblywoman Diane Harkey presented background on AB 1455 and asked the Council to support the High Speed Rail Lemon Law. Mrs. Harkey also answered questions of the City Council.
Larry Gilbert, M.V.: expressed support for Assemblywoman Harkey’s bill and asked the Council to approve the proposed resolution.
City Manager Wilberg announced that he plans to bring to the City Council a similar resolution in support of AB 985.
Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, to adopt Resolution 12-12 Supporting AB 1455 (Harkey) High Speed Rail Lemon Law.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
CONSENT CALENDAR
Items 16 and 18 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.
Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the Consent Calendar as described below.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
1.
Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions
Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.
2.
City Council Minutes
Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of February 6, 2012, as presented.
3.
Check Register Dated January 27, 2012, in the Amount of $2,563,216.20
Ratified the accompanying check register.
4.
Check Register Dated February 3, 2012, in the Amount of $898,213.01
Ratified the accompanying check register.
5.
Quarterly Check Registers and Quarterly Cash Receipts Report â?? Second Quarter of FY 2011-12
Received and filed.
6.
City Treasurer's Monthly Report for December 2011
Received and filed.
7.
Community Development Agency (CDA) Treasurer's Monthly Report for December 2011
Received and filed.
8.
Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer's Monthly Report for December 2011
Received and filed.
9.
Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer's Monthly Report for December 2011
Received and filed.
10.
Quarterly Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo - Second Quarter of 2011-12
Received and filed.
11.
Quarterly Financial Report for the Community Development Agency - Second Quarter of 2011-12
Received and filed.
12.
Semi-Annual Financial Reports for the Community Development Financing Authority - For the Six Months Ended December 31, 2011
Received and filed.
13.
Comprehensive Annual Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo for the Fiscal Year Ended June 30, 2011
Received and filed.
14.
Audit Report for the Air Quality Improvement Fund for the Fiscal Year Ended June 30, 2011 and AB 2766 Annual Program Report, FY 2010-11
Received and filed.
15.
Single Audit of Federal Grant Programs for the Fiscal Year Ended June 30, 2011
Received and filed.
17.
Successor Agency Approval of Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule (ROPS)
Adopted Resolution 12-09 Acting as the Successor Agency to the Mission Viejo Community Development Agency ("Agency") Approving the Recognized Obligation Schedule ("ROPS") and Authorizing Certain Other Actions Pursuant Section 34177 or Part 1.85 of the Dissolution Act.
PUBLIC HEARINGS
OLD BUSINESS
19.
Marguerite Tennis Center Renovation Project (CIP 501)
Director of Recreation and Community Services Kelly Doyle presented the staff report.
Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, seconded by Mayor Ury, to (1) approve Change Order No.7 to the Construction Contract with Western Alta Construction Company in an amount $11,232.38; and (2) adopt Resolution 12-10 Amending the Fiscal Year 2011-2012 Budget for Costs Related to Capital Improvement Marguerite Tennis Center Project (CIP 501) for $11,232.38.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Mayor Ury, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, Council Member Schlicht, Council Member Leckness, and Council Member Kelley
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
NEW BUSINESS
ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR
16.
Agreement for Professional Services Among the Successor Agency of Community Development Agency of the City of Mission Viejo, and the Mission Viejo Housing Authority, and the City of Mission Viejo, and Stradling Yocca Carlson & Rauth for Special Counsel Legal Services
Larry Gilbert, M.V.: recommended that the City seek bids for Special Counsel legal services in order to find the best price.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ury, to approve the Professional Services Agreement with Stradling Yocca Carlson & Rauth for Special Counsel Legal Services.
Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, to reject the contract offered by Stradling Yocca Carlson and Rauth and request that Richards Watson and Gershon submit a proposal for professional services among the Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency of the City of Mission Viejo, and the Mission Viejo Housing Authority, and the City of Mission Viejo.
Mayor Ury ruled that the motion was out of order.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
Council Member Schlicht
ABSENT:
None
18.
Purchase of Three Replacement Police Services Motorcycles for FY 2011-12
Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, to (1) issue a Purchase Order for Three Police Motorcycles to Huntington Beach Honda in the amount of $71,193; and (2) adopt Resolution 12-10 Amending the FY 2011/2012 Budget to Recognize the Insurance Reimbursement Related to the Damage of a Police Services Motorcycle and an Offsetting Appropriation to Purchase a Replacement Motorcycle.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS
20.
Appointment to the Investment Advisory Commission
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ury, to appoint Roger Cregg to the Investment Advisory Commission.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
21.
Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report
Council Member Kelley presented the report.
22.
Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Mayor Ury presented the report.
23.
San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Council Member Kelley presented the report as she attended the recent TCA meeting on Mayor Pro Tem Reardon’s behalf.
24.
SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report
Council Member Kelley presented the report.
RECESS
At the hour of 8:10 p.m., Mayor Ury declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 8:23 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.
STAFF REPORTS
City Manager’s Report
City Manager Wilberg recommended that the Council refer to Exhibit A of the SCAG report (item 24) for a listing of the taxes and new fees which would have been passed on to businesses in Mission Viejo without all of Council Member Kelley’s hard work.
City Attorney’s Report
25.
Employment Contract for Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services, W. Keith Rattay
City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.
Larry Gilbert, M.V.: stated that the contract is unnecessary and he commended Council Member Schlicht for contacting the City’s benchmark comparison cities and finding out that none of those cities have a contract with their Assistant City Manager.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to direct staff to offer the Assistant City Manager contract to Mr. Rattay for his consideration and approval or rejection.
Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, seconded by Council Member Schlicht, to direct staff to offer the Assistant City Manager contract to Mr. Rattay (A12-07) as amended. The amendment would exclude severance pay in the case of non-renewal and severance would not be granted if the Assistant City Manager, upon notice of non-renewal, were to quit (removal of Section 7B, I, II and III on page 4.) Mayor Pro Tem Reardon withdrew the motion.
Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, seconded by Council Member Schlicht, to direct staff to offer the Assistant City Manager contract to Mr. Rattay, as amended. Amendment would decrease the severance from 9 months to 6 months.
On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:
AYES:
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon.
NOES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, and Mayor Ury.
ABSENT:
None
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
Council Member Schlicht, and Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
ABSENT:
None
COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS (Continued)
26.
Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended
The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Kelley announced that she attended the opening of the Capistrano Valley High School Art Gallery on February 9. The art studio was accomplished through the hard work of the CVHS foundation as well as the teachers and students. She encouraged residents to visit the gallery to see the fine talent of the CVHS students. Council Member Kelley also attended the Chamber of Commerce Mixer at the Microsoft Store at the Shops at Mission Viejo, opening day for girls softball, and the Tribute to our Nations Heroes at Kaleidoscope Center. She noted that Petra Jewelers offered a donation back to the Wounded Warriors fund and she encouraged residents to visit Kaleidoscope and all of its businesses, including Petra. Council Member Kelley reminded that community that the Mission Viejo Activities Committee 2nd annual Up in the Air event will take place on March 3, 2012, from 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. on the Village Green at Oso Viejo Park. Admission is free and there will be arts and crafts, kites, a disc dog show, radio controlled planes and helicopters. Council Member Kelly concluded her comments by informing her colleagues that she will be out of town from February 27 through March 5, returning just prior to the Council Meeting that evening so she may be a few minutes late.
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Leckness agreed that the Chamber Mixer was a great event and he was impressed that all five Council Members were present.
Council Member Schlicht
28.
Resolution Opposing Trustee Attendance Boundaries Map J Approved by the CUSD Trustees
Council Member Schlicht presented her report.
City Attorney Curley recommended that the City Council subcommittee convene with the CUSD subcommittee to express its concerns, share the resolution and ask the reasons why the CUSD Board voted the way they did regarding the Trustee Attendance Boundaries.
Motion made by , seconded by , to
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
Council Member Schlicht announced that she didn’t appreciate the intent of Council Member Kelley’s comments regarding the CUSD boundaries and she noted that Mrs. Kelley didn’t make a motion when she brought the item to the Council originally. Council Member Schlicht announced that she attended the Lake Forest City Council meeting on February 7 where she learned that Lake Forest was able to reduce the size of its fire hazard zone maps. She also attended the MVHS girls basketball game where the Diablos defeated the Dolphins, the CVHS art gallery opening and the Diablos Cougar basketball game. Council Member Schlicht noted that the group Freedom Is Not Free is helping veterans and their families and she encouraged residents to visit www.freedomisnotfree.com for more information. She also attended the Mission Viejo Planning Commission meeting on February 13, and on Feb 16 she welcomed local business owners to the Chamber Mixer as an Ambassador. Council Member Schlicht further outlined her attendance at the Saddleback Republican Assembly meeting where she heard Congressman Jon Fleischman speak. On February 17 she cheered for the Diablos boys basketball team and on February 19 she had lunch with “President Lincoln” at the Casta Del Sol Republican Club. Council Member Schlicht reminded residents that various little league teams will hold their opening ceremonies this week and on February 27, 2012, the American Legion will host its award show to honor law enforcement personnel. She concluded by reminding residents that the Orange County Fire Authority will hold a public information meeting on the proposed Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zones in the Saddleback Room at City Hall on February 28 and on March 5, the City Council will hold a public hearing on the same subject.
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon announced that she attended most of the events that her colleagues have already outlined. She also had the pleasure of speaking with Jay Kopelman who has written a book entitled From Baghdad With Love and he is involved with Freedom is Not Free. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon encouraged residents to attend the February 28 workshop to hear OCFA staff talk about the Very High Fire Hazard Area Maps. And regarding upcoming events, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon announced that she will attend Read Across America at Castille Elementary School and she will visit the Marguerite Tennis Center to receive a status update on the construction project. She also looks forward to the Little League opening ceremonies on February 24 and 25.
Mayor Ury
29.
Aegean Hills Lake Mission Viejo Membership
Mayor Ury presented his report.
Larry Gilbert, M.V.: expressed opposition to the proposal.
Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to direct staff to facilitate discussion between Aegean Hills and Mission Viejo Lake to determine ultimate status of lake membership.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
Mayor Ury announced that he too attended Chamber Mixer and it was a lot of fun. He also thanked the Casta Del Sol Republican Club for inviting him to speak and he noted that he enjoyed the opportunity to chat with residents and reconnect with old friends. Mayor Ury outlined his attendance at the Heroes Tribute at Kaleidoscope and he stated that that it was another wonderful event.
ADJOURNMENT
At the hour of 9:44 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Monday, March 5, 2012, at 5:00 p.m.
______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
Approved at the meeting of March 05, 2012
